{{Short description|Element of an ordered vector space}}
An '''order unit''' is an element of an [[ordered vector space]] which can be used to bound all elements from above.<ref name="fuchssteiner+lusky">{{cite book|title=Convex Cones|last1=Fuchssteiner|first1=Benno|last2=Lusky|first2=Wolfgang|isbn=9780444862907|publisher=[[Elsevier]]|year=1981}}</ref> In this way (as seen in the first [[#Examples|example]] below) the order unit generalizes the unit element in the reals.

According to [[H. H. Schaefer]], "most of the ordered vector spaces occurring in analysis do not have order units."{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=230–234}}

== Definition ==

For the ordering cone <math>K \subseteq X</math> in the [[vector space]] <math>X</math>, the element <math>e \in K</math> is an order unit (more precisely a <math>K</math>-order unit) if for every <math>x \in X</math> there exists a <math>\lambda_x > 0</math> such that <math>\lambda_x e - x \in K</math> (that is, <math>x \leq_K \lambda_x e</math>).<ref name="aliprantis+tourky">{{cite book|author=Charalambos D. Aliprantis|author2=Rabee Tourky|title=Cones and Duality|isbn=9780821841464|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|year=2007}}</ref>

=== Equivalent definition ===

The order units of an ordering cone <math>K \subseteq X</math> are those elements in the [[algebraic interior]] of <math>K;</math> that is, given by <math>\operatorname{core}(K).</math><ref name="aliprantis+tourky" />

== Examples ==

Let <math>X = \R</math> be the real numbers and <math>K = \R_+ = \{x \in \R : x \geq 0\},</math> then the unit element <math>1</math> is an {{em|order unit}}.

Let <math>X = \R^n</math> and <math>K = \R^n_+ = \left\{ x_i \in \R : \text{ for all } i = 1, \ldots, n : x_i \geq 0 \right\},</math> then the unit element <math>\vec{1} = (1, \ldots, 1)</math> is an {{em|order unit}}.

Each interior point of the positive cone of an [[ordered topological vector space]] is an order unit.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=230–234}}

== Properties ==

Each order unit of an ordered TVS is interior to the positive cone for the order topology.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=230–234}}

If <math>(X, \leq)</math> is a preordered vector space over the reals with order unit <math>u,</math> then the map <math>p(x) := \inf \{ t \in \R : x \leq t u \}</math> is a [[sublinear functional]].{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}} 

== Order unit norm ==

Suppose <math>(X, \leq)</math> is an ordered vector space over the reals with order unit <math>u</math> whose order is [[Archimedean ordered vector space|Archimedean]] and let <math>U = [-u, u].</math> 
Then the [[Minkowski functional]] <math>p_U</math> of <math>U,</math> defined by <math>p_{U}(x) := \inf \{ r > 0 : x \in r [-u, u] \},</math> is a norm called the '''{{visible anchor|order unit norm}}'''. 
It satisfies <math>p_U(u) = 1</math> and the closed unit ball determined by <math>p_U</math> is equal to <math>[-u, u];</math> that is, <math>[-u, u] = \left\{ x \in X : p_U(x) \leq 1 \right\}.</math>{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}}
